headline: TODAY IS THE DAY THE RENA AGREEMENT DIES, AND THE SHOWING LANDS AT 10:30 THIS MORNING — the number is still unruled and the agent's lake-access question is still unanswered from yesterday afternoon. · DO: answer Kyle B. before 10:30, then rule the number · WATCH: The Daily never fired at 6:25 this morning — you have no letter today, and that absence is verified twice.

notes: 🔴 THE DAILY DID NOT FIRE THIS MORNING. Your 6:25 AM letter — the anchor of the whole day — never ran and never sent. This is verified two independent ways rather than assumed: there is no heartbeat line for it anywhere in today's log, and a direct search of your sent mail for it returns nothing. Every other morning routine ran on time. This is the one gap, and it is why the board is amber on a day where the fleet is otherwise healthy.

✅ THE FLEET ITSELF IS UP AND HAS RUN CLEAN SINCE MIDNIGHT — nine routine passes this morning with no gaps, nothing BLOCKED, and nothing PARTIAL. Yesterday's five-hour-forty-five-minute dark window did not repeat. The money sweep, the inbox triage, the database pull, the marketing run, the team board and three ISA sweeps all reported on time.

✅ THE PAST-CLIENT LANE CAME BACK. After staging ZERO rows two days running, it staged FIFTEEN warm check-in drafts at 5:55 this morning — and it found the reason for the failure while it was at it: a name-matching defect that had been pulling purchased-source collisions into your top tier. It moved to the verified closing registry instead. Those fifteen are sitting in your drafts waiting on you, and they are drafts by rule, not by accident.

callBlock.who: Kyle B. of eXp — he tours at 10:30 THIS MORNING and you still owe him the lake-access answer from yesterday
callBlock.why: ⏰ THIS IS THE ONLY ITEM ON THE BOARD WITH A HARD CLOCK ON IT, AND THE CLOCK IS THIS MORNING. He requested the second tour at 1:57 yesterday, it confirmed at 3:41, you sent the access instructions at 3:42, and at 3:47 he asked where the lake access is. You said you would find out. That answer is now roughly sixteen hours old and the tour is in under three. ⭐ AN AGENT WHO ASKS ABOUT AMENITIES BETWEEN BOOKING AND TOURING IS PRE-SELLING THE HOUSE TO SOMEBODY — that is the whole reason this row sits first. ⛔ ON THE SAME CALL, ASK THE ONE QUESTION THAT MATTERS: same buyers, or different ones. He texted at 8:07 yesterday morning that his buyers had to get their own house listed before looking anymore, then booked six hours later. Both cannot be true of the same buyer. ⏰ His answer arrives inside the last window where it can still change the pricing conversation you are having with the sellers TODAY.

callBlock.who: Ann & Don C. — the agreement expires TODAY and the number has still never been ruled
callBlock.why: 🔴 THIS IS THE LAST DAY. Not the last evening, not the deadline week — today. ⭐ THE EXTENSION IS SETTLED AND MUST NOT BE RE-OPENED: you emailed the ask 8/12 and told them in writing the decision is due Friday. Only the number is open. 🔴 THE EVIDENCE MOVED IN ONE DIRECTION YESTERDAY AND IT HAS NOT MOVED BACK: the 8/11 full-price showing that this board treated for two days as the strongest argument against repricing NEVER HAPPENED — the agent said so himself, he did not have time to see it. The counter-argument was never real. ⭐ WHAT IS REAL: eighty-nine days at this price, exactly one written offer all summer, and the co-op agent volunteered that figure as their client's ceiling. ⚠️ THE SEQUENCING QUESTION IS NOW SHARPER THAN IT WAS LAST NIGHT, BECAUSE THE TOUR IS TODAY: reprice before 10:30 so the tour sees the new number, or let the tour happen and rule at noon with one more read in hand. Both orderings are defensible and this desk is not ruling for you. ⛔ An expired agreement is a closing you already paid for and handed back.

callBlock.who: Robert — the buyer who left a voicemail on Rena yesterday morning asking for workshop photos
callBlock.why: 🔥 A BUYER CALLED YOU DIRECTLY AT 9:33 YESTERDAY MORNING AND ASKED FOR MORE PICTURES OF THE WORKSHOP AND GARAGE. That is not a lead form — that is a person who has already studied the listing closely enough to know what is missing from it. ⏰ IT IS NOW ROUGHLY TWENTY-TWO HOURS OLD. It sat seven and a half hours yesterday because the voicemail arrives from a carrier address the sweep's standing query could not see; that defect was found and fixed last night, so the delay is a known cost rather than an ongoing one. ⭐ TWO INDEPENDENT BUYER SIGNALS ON THE SAME HOUSE IN ONE DAY, on a listing that has produced one offer all summer — and both of them landed the day before the agreement expires. ⛔ Call him and send the photos before you rule the price, not after.

callBlock.who: Gloria F. — two voicemails in one night, and the tenant answer she asked for is now twenty days owed
callBlock.why: 🔴 SHE ESCALATED THREE TIMES IN TWENTY-SEVEN MINUTES ON WEDNESDAY NIGHT — two voicemails and a text — and this is a client who had already waited nineteen days without complaining. ⭐ THE OWED THING IS YOURS, NOT HERS: she asked whether the tenant on her unit is out. You told her he had said he would call and had not. She came back with the part that matters — he owes another month's rent if he isn't out. ⚠️ YOU DO NOT NEED AN ANSWER TO MAKE THIS CALL, AND WAITING FOR ONE IS EXACTLY WHAT TURNED SIX DAYS INTO TWENTY. 'Still no word from him, here's exactly what I'm doing about it' beats a twenty-first day of silence. ⭐ She is not a loose end — she closed with you in June, still opens your market reports, and has an unclosed valuation loop on the same address.

callBlock.who: Chesley C. — his voicemail from Tuesday is now three days unreturned, and he is your cleanest deal
callBlock.why: ⚠️ THE ODD PART IS WHO THIS IS. This is not a cold lead — this is the seller on the file this board calls the cleanest on your board, with both the inspection and the appraisal already behind it and a close receipted for 8/28. ⭐ A CLIENT MID-TRANSACTION WHO CALLS AND GETS NOTHING BACK FOR THREE DAYS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE KIND OF SILENCE YOU CAN BUY, because it costs the referral, not the closing. ⚠️ There is also live business on the same file: your transaction manager reported Wednesday that he had 'forgotten' about the payoff he was ordering, which weakens the one item still keeping this deal from being called clean.

callBlock.who: Cassie C. and Angela B. — the two agents who called Comanche too high and STILL don't know it came down
callBlock.why: 🔴 BOTH CHIPS ARE NOW SIX DAYS OVERDUE, AND THE CASE GOT STRONGER AGAIN. Cassie's buyer toured 7/25, wrote the offer, and called the old ask too high. Angela's buyer toured 8/2, said interested YES, and called the same old ask too high. Neither has ever been told the price moved. ⭐ THE PATTERN SINCE THE CUT IS FOUR READS DEEP AND UNBROKEN: one agent called the new number JUST RIGHT with a 5-of-5, and the most recent read did not argue price at all — it argued the stairs. ⭐ THAT IS THE SCRIPT: the number changed, a peer validated it, and across seven reads not one person has ever named a different number. ⚠️ Honestly stated — Cassie's is a re-open of a dead deal at twenty days and that buyer may be under contract elsewhere. Both are still the cheapest at-bats you own. ⛔ Quote the current list price only. ⛔ Call, don't email — buyer's agents are the red lane under your own 8/7 rule.

callBlock.who: Clint K. — he asked you a question on 8/3 and it has never been answered
callBlock.why: ⚠️ ELEVEN DAYS. This is not a lead who went quiet — this is a person who asked you something directly and has been waiting since the first week of the month. ⭐ AN UNANSWERED DIRECT QUESTION IS A DIFFERENT CATEGORY FROM A COLD FOLLOW-UP, and it is the category that quietly ends relationships. It costs one call and no selling. ⏰ Eleven days is past the point where 'sorry for the delay' does the work on its own — lead with the answer instead.

callBlock.who: Savannah R. — she filed BOTH home-value forms thirty-eight seconds apart and volunteered detail nobody asked for
callBlock.why: 🔥 STILL THE FRESHEST SELLER SIGNAL IN THE BOOK AND IT IS NOW A DAY OLD. Someone who fills out both seller forms in under a minute — and volunteers detail about outbuildings unprompted — is describing a property they have already decided to sell. ⚠️ HER FIRST TOUCH WENT OUT FIVE HOURS AND ELEVEN MINUTES LATE because the instant responder was inside Wednesday's outage when she raised her hand. ⭐ THAT MAKES THE VOICE CALL MORE URGENT, NOT LESS — a cold email five hours behind is exactly the gap a phone call closes, and it has now been overnight on top of that.

listings.note: ⏰ EVERYTHING ON THIS FILE LANDS IN THE NEXT FEW HOURS. This board carried it for two days as the strongest evidence against repricing, and it was never real. ⭐ WHAT SURVIVES: day 89, no price change since May, exactly one written offer in that time, and the co-op agent volunteered that figure as their client's ceiling. Both feedback forms this house has ever produced left every price field BLANK; the objections were the upstairs bathroom and a compartmentalized interior. Nobody who walked it said the number was wrong. ⚠️ REPRICE BEFORE 10:30 SO THE TOUR SEES THE NEW NUMBER, OR HOLD AND RULE AT NOON WITH ONE MORE READ — both sequences are defensible; this desk is not ruling it. ⭐ THE EXTENSION IS ALREADY RULED and must not be re-asked. 🔥 A SECOND BUYER SIGNAL LANDED THE SAME DAY: a buyer left a voicemail yesterday at 9:33 asking for photos of the workshop and garage, still unreturned at roughly twenty-two hours. ⚠️ Quote $450,000 only until they rule.

Both chips have been overdue since 8/8. ⚠️ NOBODY HAS EVER NAMED A REPLACEMENT NUMBER — every price-recommendation field across all seven reads came back blank. ⛔ Quote $295,000 only. ⛔ Call, don't email. ⚠️ One open thread from the 8/10 tour: the buyer's agent asked in writing whether the ceiling stains came from a previous leak, and no answer is on record.

listings.note: ✅ THE INSPECTION RAN AND CLOSED AT 12:53 YESTERDAY AFTERNOON. ✅ THE SELLERS WERE PREPPED AND CONFIRMED — your transaction manager emailed the prep list Tuesday, texted both sellers, and confirmed Thursday morning. That standing worry is retired. ⏰ THE NEXT REAL EVENT IS A DOCUMENT AND IT STILL HAS NOT ARRIVED: no repair request, no inspection-response addendum, nothing, with the buyers' response clock now running into its second day. ⭐ THE HEADLINE NUMBER STILL DESERVES SAYING OUT LOUD: contract at $390,000 against a $380,000 list — TEN THOUSAND ABOVE ASK, inside three weeks. Your own 7/17 note had warned these sellers that taking the top of the band 'may extend sales time.' It did not, and that is the best possible thing to have been wrong about. 🔴 THE LIVE ITEM IS THE BUYER SIDE: they have questions, you offered a phone call Wednesday evening, and it has still not connected. ⚠️ Now that the report exists, that call is more urgent, not less — unanswered questions plus a fresh report is exactly how a repair demand gets written. ⭐ One thing worth telling the sellers before closing: they cleared out three times in thirty hours during the showing burst without a word of complaint. Sellers who do that are sellers who give referrals.

listings.status: ✅ Under contract $899K — close date corrected to Thursday 8/20
listings.note: ✅ TODAY IS THE DAY THE OLD STALE DATE WOULD HAVE FIRED, AND IT WILL NOT. This row said for a day that the close was receipted for 8/14 with nothing seen since 8/4. The date itself was the error: the milestone engine caught it Thursday morning and corrected 8/14 → 8/20, double-receipted off a live calendar event naming the closing attorney, the buyers and the buyer's agent, plus an executed addendum from 8/12 that names this exact field as the stale figure being carried. ⭐ HAD IT STOOD, THIS MORNING'S RUN WOULD HAVE FIRED A CLOSING CELEBRATION AND A REFERRAL SCRIPT SIX DAYS EARLY on a file still sitting at appraisal. That is the catch working. ⭐ WHAT REMAINS VERIFIED AND GOOD: the appraisal is complete and clean on the lender's own words, the repair addendum is fully executed, and the septic inspection ran 8/4. ⭐ CLOSING IS THURSDAY 8/20 AT 3:00 PM at the closing attorney's office. ⚠️ Do not re-print 8/14 anywhere — that number is retired.

listings.status: 🎉 Under contract $162K — inspection held, and a late read came in calling the price JUST RIGHT

The paragraph-30 flag is off the board. ⭐ THE FILE'S BACKSTORY IS WORTH KEEPING: the buyer's agent said her client 'really, really liked it' but needed to save more for a down payment, and this desk argued for two weeks against reading that as a price signal — she had written JUST RIGHT on the same form. She wrote. Offer to acceptance in twenty-eight minutes. Patience was the right call and it is on the record. ⭐ Closing 9/14.

listings.note: ✅ STILL THE CLEANEST FILE ON YOUR BOARD ON PAPER. Both gates are behind you: the inspection ran 8/5 at noon and the appraisal ran 8/7 at 9:00 AM, both confirmed on primary notices. ⭐ AN INSPECTION AND AN APPRAISAL BOTH SPENT IS THE STRONGEST POSITION ANY DEAL ON THIS BOARD OCCUPIES. 🔴 AND YET THE SELLER HAS BEEN WAITING ON A RETURNED CALL SINCE TUESDAY — three days, mid-transaction, on the deal with the least to worry about. Ordered is not received-by-title, and forgotten is not ordered. ⚠️ THE APPRAISED VALUE STILL HAS NOT COME BACK — now day eight with no number, reported as a single-source observation rather than an alarm. It is worth one call to the lender rather than another day of waiting. ⚠️ ONE ADMINISTRATIVE THREAD WAS LEFT UNSIGNED ON 8/4 — an address-correction addendum that sat on the signing platform without a receipt. ⚠️ One number remains unruled and it is worth real money on an otherwise settled deal: the buyer's agent asked for a specific co-op commission and nobody has ever answered.

listings.status: 🔥 Active $184K — a 'VERY interested' buyer is now six days unworked

One answered the interest question with the single word 'Very' — every other field blank, which is exactly why it needs a phone call: the enthusiasm is on record and the reason is not. ✅ THE $5,000 CUT THE SELLER APPROVED IN JULY IS VERIFIED LIVE AND PUBLIC — the MLS line on all three notices reads $184,000, so the old do-not-quote hedge is retired. 🔴 THE REAL FINDING IS THE OBJECTION AND IT IS VERIFIED THREE WAYS: the problem is SIZE, not price. The clearest read says it in four words — 'Just too small.' ⛔ NO DISCOUNT REACHES A SIZE OBJECTION. The answer here is AUDIENCE, not number — first-time buyers, downsizers, investors — and a price conversation with this seller would be solving the wrong problem. This board argued for a cut here for weeks on the strength of silence; the showings arrived and said something different, and that earlier read is withdrawn. 🔴 The ad on this listing has produced zero leads in twelve days after being the best performer on record in July.

listings.note: 🆕 THE SELLER MOVED THE NUMBER — $559,000 down to $550,000, logged by the milestone engine on three separate passes and acknowledged by you. ⚠️ A price change is not a deal advance and nothing fired on it. ⚠️ SOURCE NOTE, STATED PLAINLY: this is one source seen repeatedly, not two independent sources, and every ShowingTime notice on file still prints $559,000 because they all predate the cut. Confirm against MLS before it goes on anything client-facing. ✅ IT KEPT PRODUCING TRAFFIC THROUGH THE ENTIRE DARK WINDOW — a tour 8/4 and another 8/10 at 2:00, on a listing that has taken forty showings all-time and was relisted after the prior contract was mutually released. ⚠️ THE 8/4 READ IS THE FIRST ONE THAT HURTS: interested No · priced TOO HIGH · staging 2 out of 5. ⭐ THE STAGING SCORE IS THE ACTIONABLE HALF, NOT THE PRICE HALF. A 2 is the lowest this listing has ever recorded, against a 4 three weeks earlier from an agent who called the price JUST RIGHT — the house did not get more expensive between those two visits, it got less presentable. 🔴 AND IT CORROBORATES AN ITEM THIS BOARD HAS CARRIED UNACTIONED FOR THREE WEEKS: the 7/23 read said dirty plus GLITCHING ELECTRICAL. An electrician and a cleaner are still cheaper than another lost buyer. ⚠️ The 8/10 tour is now four days silent with no feedback returned.

listings.note: 🆕 FOUR BUYER SIGNALS IN THREE DAYS WHILE EVERY OTHER AD IN THE PORTFOLIO PRODUCED ZERO. This is currently the only marketing spend that is working, which makes how the leads are handled the real question — and both named land leads still have no call logged against them. 🔴 THE BUILDER'S PERC QUESTION IS NOW FOUR DAYS OLD AND STILL BLOCKED: your transaction manager spent five and a half hours on it and reports the county will not search the septic records without a per-lot fee across all nineteen lots. She is stopped until you rule, and she has now been stopped overnight. ⭐ THERE IS A FREE PATH AND IT SHOULD BE TRIED FIRST — ask the developer for the perc results directly; a developer who platted the subdivision almost certainly has them, and it costs a phone call instead of a search fee. ⚠️ THAT QUESTION IS THE GATE ON THE WHOLE PACKAGE — perc results decide buildability, buildability decides price per lot, and a builder who gets no answer assumes the worst. ⚠️ TWO BUILDER OUTREACH ADDRESSES ARE BOUNCING, found in this morning's triage — so part of the builder audience for this package is not receiving anything at all. ⭐ Blocks and takedowns at a higher per-lot number remain acceptable per the seller's own ruling.

listings.note: ✅ THE PRICE QUESTION THIS BOARD CARRIED AS UNVERIFIED IS ANSWERED — you ruled $185,000, so the number is quotable and the old hedge is retired. ⏰ THE SEQUENCING PROBLEM IS NOW A WEEKEND PROBLEM: the sellers asked for the photographer on MONDAY, and the listing agreement went out for signature but is still NOT SIGNED. Today is the last business day before that shoot. Booking against an unsigned agreement is exactly how a shoot slips — and this same sequence already cost time on the Deer Ridge file. ⭐ THE MOVE IS ONE CONVERSATION, NOT TWO: close the signature and confirm the shoot in the same call, today. ⚠️ A note from the milestone engine worth carrying: this file has been sitting at ACTIVE in the state tracker since 6/19 while the sellers are only now asking for photos — it was almost certainly seeded to the wrong stage, so treat it as pre-launch. ⭐ Worth remembering what this relationship actually is: she came in unprompted off a listing alert saying they were very interested in a property AND about ready to list their own. This is the LIST half of a two-sided deal, and the BUY half has still never been worked.

On a listing that had gone 126 days with essentially no traffic, that brief burst was the only real activity this file has produced and it has fully decayed. ⚠️ A PRICE DISCREPANCY OPENED DURING THE DARK WINDOW AND IS STILL FLAGGED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: the last primary source this desk holds prints one number and a routine's later summary carries another, five thousand apart. ⛔ NEITHER IS QUOTABLE UNTIL THE MLS IS READ DIRECTLY — one of them is stale and this desk cannot tell which. ⭐ THE GOOD NEWS ON THIS FILE IS STILL UNDELIVERED AT FOURTEEN DAYS, WHICH MAKES IT THE OLDEST OWED ITEM ON THE BOARD: the 7/31 read came back interested No, but with the price called JUST RIGHT, a 4-of-5 rating, and the comment that the buyers prefer the east end of the beach although they liked this complex. That is a GEOGRAPHY loss, not a price loss, and it is the only independent validation of this list price the file has ever carried. ⭐ He is out of state and lives on these reads. Lead with the price answer, not the no.

listings.note: ⚠️ THE LARGEST NUMBER ON YOUR BOARD IS STILL THE ONE WITH THE WEAKEST FILE.
